html:
The Nauset were an Algonquian people of outer Cape Cod in Massachusetts, east of the Bass River. They were closely related to the Wampanoag and usually deferred to the Wampanoag chief sachem, but kept their own sachems.

They met Europeans early. In 1605 Samuel de Champlain explored their coast and his men clashed with them. In 1614 the English captain Thomas Hunt kidnapped Nauset and Patuxet men to sell as slaves in Spain. So when the Pilgrims came ashore in 1620, the Nauset shot at them, in what the English called the First Encounter. They soon made peace with Plymouth Colony, and many became Christians in "praying towns". Most stayed out of King Philip's War in 1675. Epidemics and land loss shrank them, and their descendants joined the Mashpee community.
